fields.Name: IT132 - FLS Close-out (cache segmentation, RunQuery)
fields.Description: Field-level security close-out checks for server cache segmentation and saved-query enforcement. Server transport, reusing the fls-enforcement fixture plus Reader.Email Deny. Cache segmentation by field-security fingerprint: PC1 a restricted user's cold miss does not narrow the result an unrestricted user then gets for the same request; PC2 a restricted user is never served a slot an unrestricted user warmed — its read writes its own segment and carries no denied value; PC3 a UserSearchString that matches a row only through a column the reader is denied returns the row to the unrestricted user and never to the reader, even after the unrestricted user warmed the identical request (the column is added to the user-search field set through the entity path for the check and restored afterwards). Saved queries enforce FLS: PQ1 a saved query selecting a denied column is refused for the restricted caller and runs for the unrestricted one; PQ2 a saved query filtering on a denied column is refused even though it selects only allowed ones; PQ3 a saved query reading whole rows (SELECT *) fails closed for the restricted caller; PQ4 a query whose role list includes the restricted caller's role runs for that caller (role-list grants bypass FLS by design). fls-enforcement FLS11 now asserts the same segmented behaviour from the ordinary-read side. Fixture queries are created under a throwaway category with the AI enrichment step skipped and deleted with their permission rows in teardown.

ExpectedOutcomes.summary: Server cache slots are segmented by field-security fingerprint (no narrowing, no wide serving, no row-set leak through search), and saved queries that read a denied column in any clause are refused for a restricted caller unless a role-list grant covers them.
